comments.author: Claudia
comments.body:
It really depends on whether you ONLY want to grind SP, or if you also want to work on your tech levels. If you find a good spot with 3-4 mobs spawning close together, you can efficiently grind without a break, and you'll also collect a lot of swmp and other stuff, which helps offset the dura costs.

I can't think of a reason that one would try to avoid working on their tech levels. Sitting there hacking at a mob without killing it seems silly and counterproductive to me, especially when you can turn a (smallish) profit by grinding normally.

comments.author: Meng Meng
comments.body:
You do not want to use attack items like boomerangs, although you could use items that paralyze or blind. Doing damage with items is counter productive.

Also, you want to use a very low damage weapon, on a mob that takes a long time to kill that way, but won't do too much damage to you in the process. That way you can keep hacking away at it for skill prof, and not waste time going to other mobs, waiting for battle to start again, etc. With enough defense, there's no reason you can't beat on a mob for a LONG time, as long as your damage is low enough that they keep healing.

Don't bother with mobs below your level. Go for the strongest mob that can't hurt you too much (this is where good armour comes in). The increased xp that higher level mobs give is mitigated by not killing them nearly as often.

comments.author: Chester
comments.body: In a nutshell, what you want to do is go with a fleet of people who all want to grind techs. You decide which colour of tech you'll grind, and disable all other colours, traps, whatever. You circle a strong mob, use very weak weapons, and let your techs build up. Then, you do a huge chain, which at best means each person gets a chain of like, 12 to 14. That gives upwards of 100 points to that colour of tech, so 5 of those means a tech level.

comments.author: Dongwoo
comments.body:
If you are just looking at the xp equation then land battles are faster early on. however, this is a sailing game so eventually it's better xp to go out to sea. Now the question is how serious do you want to be about sea battles? every level of maritime you get on land means your sea battle skills are lagging further and further behind.

If however you are a trader and you just need maritime levels to get into ships or you're a bit more hardcore and you want more skill slots and court ranks, then a very viable alternative is to do land battles to level 52, get yourself in a vaisseau, and go deck battle. It's risky because deck battling can take a few rounds to take, but it gets you a load of maritime xp in a hurry, and it works for arms skill prof.

comments.author: H.-Gazi
comments.body:
***Extra Information***
This skill raises the attack power in melee battle by +3 per rank and for land battle +2~+3 per rank for close-ranged weapons. These weapons are: Sword, Ax, Club/Staff and Spear.

It can be grinded during melee battle, but doing land battle with close-ranged weapons is way faster. You can proficiency per hit you cause with you weapon and it is currently unknown for me if the levels of NPC has influence on it. It is not hard to max this.

This skill is also very essential for obtaining R2+ battle-techs (including the R1 Trick) and +boosters may work when trying.

Since the Gran Atlas it is possible to refine this skill and I highly recommend it to do this. It will give the following effects:

1) Reset to rank 1 in exchange for permanent +2 boost.
2) Required proficiency is reduced by 20%.
3) Secundaire effect: Reduces the vigour consume for using melee skills by 10%.

Hope this makes clears for the most of you. :-)

King Regards,

Huseyin-Gazi
